question: _______ means the transfer of ownership, management and control of public sector enterprises to the private sector.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Privatisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Privatisation refers to the transfer of ownership, management, and control of public sector enterprises to the private sector.
 
• The main objective of privatisation is to improve efficiency and productivity by involving private sector participation.
 
• It often involves the sale of government-owned assets or stock to private entities.
 
• Privatisation can lead to increased competition, better customer service, and innovation due to private sector management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digitalisation**

 
 
• Digitalisation refers to the use of digital technologies to change a business model and provide new revenue and value-producing opportunities.
 
• It is the process of moving to a digital business.
 
• Digitalisation involves the conversion of information into a digital format.
 
• This term is often used in the context of the digital transformation of business and society.
 
 
 
• **Globalisation**
 
 
• Globalisation is the process of interaction and integration among people, companies, and governments worldwide.
 
• It involves the international exchange of goods, services, information, technology, and cultural practices.
 
• Globalisation has led to increased economic interdependence and the global spread of technology and innovation.
 
• It can have both positive and negative impacts on economies, societies, and cultures.
 
 
 
• **Liberalisation**
 
 
• Liberalisation refers to the relaxation of government restrictions, usually in areas of social, political, and economic policy.
 
• In the context of economic policy, it means reducing state intervention in the economy.
 
• Liberalisation can include measures like reducing tariffs, deregulating markets, and encouraging foreign investment.
 
• It aims to create a more competitive and efficient economic environment.
